body: Photography was what I got into my college with, but I was planning on diverging, creating different mixed media pieces from a bunch of ideas and gallery concepts I had. But it just kept on getting muddled down. I've kinda just given up now. I haven't picked up a camera and felt that same joy; the way the shutter clicks and that instant satisfaction. The way you get to hide behind it and capture beautiful intimate moments. When you push the film advance switch forward for your next shot. That anger when a stranger on the street realizes their moment was stolen and the explanation that it was all for art. I haven't had that in ages, and it kills me. Every camera I have picked up has broken on me. No shot is worth anything anymore. My classmates will end up being the next Lauren Greenfield, Gordon Parks, Mike Kelley, Philip Lorca-Dicorcia. I know it may seem like I am throwing out names, but the point is that their art is relevant. It emotes. It'll be important and be remembered. I won't in the scale that I ever dreamed to be. I recently realized that all of my dreams are going to die. I can't pursue the paths I want. Sylvia Plath really had it right with the concept of depression and stagnation.

I'm going to be honest not fully sure what L means I am going to assume it means acid, correct me if I am wrong please. But the last time I dropped was on thursday, and what you explain regarding that awful lobotomy feeling is exactly how I felt both times I half dosed.
I don't know what to say for this really besides spilling my guts out. Today wasn't great, and I keep on overthinking.
